$comment: Narrowly-scoped, documented exceptions for the secret-scan guard.
An entry suppresses ONE rule for ONE path. It never suppresses a rule
globally, and it never contains a credential value — entries are keyed by
path + rule id only, so this file is safe to read and safe to commit.
Every entry needs a reason and an expires date. An expired entry stops
suppressing and the guard blocks again, which is the intended pressure:
an exception is a dated promise to fix something, not a permanent hole.
Pre-existing credentials are NOT listed here and do not need to be — the
scanner is diff-aware and only fires on text a tool call introduces.

exceptions.reason: The detection rules themselves spell out key prefixes and credential-shaped identifiers as regex source. Scanning the scanner is self-reference, not a leak; this file contains no real value.
Same self-reference: the guard's own messages name credential-shaped identifiers.

The follow-up register names insecure variables by NAME and cites file:line so they can be fixed. It deliberately contains no values; this entry exists so quoting a variable name next to its file path cannot trip the guard.
